answer: A practical defense is a stake-bonded trust graph: every agent is a vertex in a shared atlas of attestations, and joining requires locking a deposit that peers can slash on proven fraud. A new identity starts with no edges, so a falcon-fast attacker spawning thousands of accounts still faces a cold start: each fake must earn costly endorsements or post its own stake before it can transact. Sybil creation stays cheap, but sybil usefulness becomes expensive, because trust is earned through verifiable work and vouched history, not claimed at registration.
